questions.question: Isobars are lines joining places with equal:
Why does a high-pressure cell generally bring clear, settled weather?
options: Because air rises and cools in a high
Because air sinks in a high, warming and drying as it descends
Because highs only occur in summer
Because highs contain no air movement

questions.question: Closely packed isobars on a synoptic chart indicate:
options: Strong winds due to a steep pressure gradient

questions.question: A station circle shaded six-eighths means:
options: Six-eighths of the sky is covered in cloud
There is a 6/8 chance of rain

questions.question: Air temperature 18 °C, dew point 16 °C. What does the small gap tell you?
options: The station is at high altitude
The air is nearly saturated — humid, with condensation or rain close at hand

questions.question: A wind shaft flying into the circle from the north-west with two full feathers represents:
options: A wind blowing toward the north-west at 10 knots

questions.question: Winds are always named according to:
On a synoptic chart a cold front is drawn as a line with:
options: Triangles pointing in the direction the front is moving

questions.question: South African cold fronts typically approach from the:
Why do towering cumulonimbus clouds build along the cold front line?
options: The dense cold air wedges under the warm air and forces it violently upward, where it cools and condenses
The warm air sinks below the cold air
The front blocks all wind movement
High pressure at the front squeezes clouds together

questions.question: Which station-model reading is the classic PRE-frontal picture ahead of a South African cold front?
options: Cold south-westerly wind with clearing skies
Dry air with a 20-degree dew point gap
Warm, humid north-westerly flow with thickening cloud

subtopics.title: The Weather Behind the Front — and the Exam Method

questions.question: Which trio describes the weather BEHIND a cold front?
As a cold front passes a station, the wind typically swings from:
After the front passes, atmospheric pressure at the station:
options: Rises as the low moves away and the next high builds in

questions.question: The lesson's exam method insists that answers be given 'in observations, not vibes'. This means:
options: Describing how the weather feels emotionally
Avoiding all numbers in your answer
Quoting the numbers, naming the wind directions, citing the symbols as evidence

subtopics.title: Highs, Lows and Which Way the Air Is Going

questions.question: In a high-pressure cell the air is:
In the kettle comparison, why is the steam invisible right at the spout and visible a few centimetres higher?
options: It has risen and cooled, so its moisture condenses into visible cloud

questions.question: Isobars squeezed close together mean:
options: A steep pressure landscape, so the air runs down it fast — strong wind

questions.question: Which two-word pairs summarise the pressure cells correctly?

subtopics.title: The Little Circle That Holds a Whole Weather Report

questions.question: If the sky is cut into eight slices and six of them hold cloud, the station circle is:
A cold cooldrink bottle 'sweats' on a summer day because:
options: The air touching the cold glass is cooled to its dew point and gives up its moisture
The glass is warmer than the air

questions.question: Temperature 25 °C with a dew point of 5 °C describes air that is:
options: Very dry — it must cool 20 degrees before anything condenses

questions.question: A shaft with two full feathers flying in from the north-west tells you:
options: The wind blows toward the north-west at 2 knots
The station recorded 2 mm of rain
A north-westerly wind at 20 knots, about 37 km/h

subtopics.title: Before, During and After the Cold Front

questions.question: Why does the cold air slide UNDER the warm air at a front?
options: Because cold air is heavier than warm air
Because the ground pushes it down

questions.question: In the 'three witnesses' test, a station reporting a south-westerly wind tells you:
options: The front is still on its way

questions.question: Which set of readings says 'the front is still coming'?
options: Clear sky, easterly wind, pressure steady
Cold and showery with clearing skies
18 °C, north-westerly wind, thickening cloud, pressure falling

questions.question: After a front sweeps the Cape, when does the same cold air usually reach Bloemfontein and Gauteng?
options: A day or two later, as a cold snap
Never — fronts stop at the coast
